title: Installing Software
objective: Learn how to search for, install, and manage software packages using the apt package manager.
explanation: On your phone, you install apps from the App Store or Google Play. On Linux, you install software using a package manager. On Raspberry Pi and other Debian-based systems (like Ubuntu), the package manager is called apt. A package is simply a bundle that contains a program and everything it needs to run. The package manager downloads it from an online repository, installs it, and keeps track of it so you can update or remove it later. Before installing anything, you should always run sudo apt update first. This command refreshes the list of available packages so your system knows about the latest versions. It does not install anything — it just updates the catalog. Think of it like refreshing a shopping website to see new products. To search for software, use apt search followed by a keyword. For example, apt search image editor shows you all packages related to image editing. The list can be long, so you might want to pipe it into grep to narrow it down. Once you find what you want, install it with sudo apt install followed by the package name. For example, sudo apt install htop installs htop, a beautiful process viewer that is much nicer than plain top. You need sudo because installing software changes system files. When apt asks 'Do you want to continue?', type y and press Enter. To remove software you no longer need, use sudo apt remove followed by the package name. If you want to update all installed software to their latest versions, run sudo apt upgrade after doing sudo apt update. This is how you keep your Raspberry Pi secure and up to date. It is a good habit to run update and upgrade regularly, perhaps once a week. The package manager is one of the best things about Linux. Instead of searching random websites for downloads, everything comes from a trusted, centralized source.

commands.description: Refreshes the list of available packages from the online repositories. Always do this before installing.
commands.expectedOutput:
Hit:1 http://archive.raspberrypi.org/debian bookworm InRelease
Hit:2 http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm InRelease
Reading package lists... Done
Building dependency tree... Done
commands.troubleshooting: If you see 'Could not resolve' errors, check your internet connection with 'ping google.com'.

commands.description: Searches for packages matching 'htop'. You do not need sudo for searching.
commands.expectedOutput:
Sorting... Done
Full Text Search... Done
htop/stable 3.2.2-2 arm64
  interactive processes viewer
commands.troubleshooting: If the search returns too many results, add '| grep <keyword>' to narrow it down.

commands.description: Installs the htop package. Apt downloads it and sets everything up automatically.

commands.troubleshooting: If you see 'Unable to locate package', run 'sudo apt update' first, then try again. Check the package name spelling.

challenge.question: Install the program 'cowsay' (it makes a cow say things in your terminal). Then run it with: cowsay Hello Linux! What commands do you need?
challenge.hint: First update with sudo apt update, then install with sudo apt install cowsay.

funFact: The Debian Linux repository has over 59,000 packages — all free! That is more apps than most app stores. And the name 'Debian' comes from its creator Ian Murdock and his girlfriend Debra: Deb + Ian = Debian.
